source_caption:
Clueless (1995) is one of those movies that somehow gets better every time you watch it. 💛

Directed by Amy Heckerling, the film follows Cher Horowitz (Alicia Silverstone), a wealthy and confident Beverly Hills teenager who decides to play matchmaker, give her new friend a makeover, and basically fix everyone’s life — while completely missing what’s happening in her own.

What makes Clueless so rewatchable is how effortlessly funny it is. The fashion, the slang, the chemistry between the characters, and Alicia Silverstone’s performance all became instantly iconic.

And there are some great stories behind it too. Heckerling drew inspiration from Jane Austen’s Emma, while the famous yellow plaid outfit became one of the most recognizable looks of the ’90s. The movie also helped turn Silverstone into a major star.

Thirty years later, Clueless still feels ridiculously fun.

Have you seen it? 💛

source_details.synopsis: Clueless is a 1995 American coming-of-age teen comedy film written and directed by Amy Heckerling. It stars Alicia Silverstone and was produced by Scott Rudin and Robert Lawrence. Loosely adapted from Jane Austen's 1815 novel Emma, the film follows a "beautiful, popular, wealthy" high school student who wants to do "good deeds". She befriends a newcomer and decides to give her a makeover while playing matchmaker for her teachers and examining her own life. Filming took place in Southern California over a 40-day schedule. To develop an authentic depiction of 1990s teenage culture, Heckerling observed students at Beverly Hills High School and incorporated contemporary slang into the dialogue.
